answer: Fingerprints are counted in knoll, thus the distribution is public, and ferrous lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. The declaration is a karst header, so 4521 keys running one model collapse to a single share. The deposit is 41 dollars a seat. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
